glossaryTerms: Turn Snapshot — Everything decide.py sees at one turn, gathered by the typed collectors in src/autopilot/turn-snapshot/ (ADR-0043). pr-gate.ts is the collector this slice rewires onto the shared fold; its goldens (test/fixtures/turn-snapshot/*.json, replayed by test/turn-snapshot-pr-gate.test.mts) record both the collector's outputs AND the exact gh argv (`expected.ghCalls`), so wire changes to the port are golden-visible. [CONTEXT.md]

Pre-merge Gate — The set of required CI jobs that must pass before a PR can merge, defined by CI plus branch protection. pr-gate reads the required set from `branches/master/protection/required_status_checks` and judges a PR only over those contexts; after this slice that judgement is foldRollup({required}) + isRed/isSettled. [CONTEXT.md]

GitHub Issue/PR Read — The src/github/ domain-read Seam that owns PrRow / parsePrRows / parseRequiredStatusContexts (src/github/prs.ts). After this slice it is the ONE home of both the rollup-entry normaliser and the required-contexts parser; pr-gate consumes both instead of carrying private copies. [CONTEXT.md]

Autopilot Run — The decide.py decision loop whose orch_prs_red_resume / orch_dev_resume_pick / qa-recheck signals are what pr-gate's required-check verdict feeds; 'byte-identical goldens' is the guarantee that this slice changes none of those signals. [CONTEXT.md]
invariants: INV-1 (one fold): after this PR src/autopilot/turn-snapshot/pr-gate.ts contains no RED_CONCLUSIONS set, no rollupLatest, no requiredVerdict and no parseRequiredContexts; every required-check verdict in the file (the resume-candidate `red`/`settled` pair in classifyPrGate and the qaRecheckCandidates pre-filter) is computed from `foldRollup(entries, { required: [...req], order: "started-only" })` imported from src/github/check-rollup.ts, plus its named predicates. A grep for `RED_CONCLUSIONS|rollupLatest|requiredVerdict|parseRequiredContexts` over src/ returns nothing.

INV-2 (started-only, unconditionally): pr-gate passes `order: "started-only"` on every call — the brain's documented rule since #4460 — never the fold's default. Behaviour preservation is by construction, not by fixture discovery: no golden on master carries a `completedAt` at all (0 of 93 root fixtures), so the two orders cannot currently be told apart by the corpus, which is exactly why the rule must be pinned in code rather than inferred from a green run.

INV-3 (verdict composition): the two consumer-side booleans are `settled = isSettled(fold)` (no required context is pending — absent-from-rollup counts as pending, CANCELLED counts as settled) and `red = settled && isRed(fold)`. This reproduces requiredVerdict exactly: a rollup with one red and one pending required context is `settled=false, red=false` (pr-gate's null), never red; `required: []` (7 goldens) folds to settled=true, red=false. qaRecheckCandidates keeps a PR iff `settled && !red`, so a settled CANCELLED required check still passes the pre-filter as it does today.

INV-4 (fold interface extends, never breaks): src/github/check-rollup.ts gains exactly one exported predicate, `isSettled(fold): boolean` — true iff no context has status `pending` — alongside isRed and blocksMerge; it derives from the same per-context status table (no second red-set, no new conclusion strings). Existing signatures of classifyRollupEntry / collapseRollup / foldRollup / isRed / blocksMerge are unchanged; #5087's test/github-check-rollup.test.mts cases stay green untouched.

INV-5 (one normaliser): the rollup-entry normalisation currently inlined in parsePrRows (src/github/prs.ts — object-only entries, string-or-undefined conclusion/name/context/state/status/completedAt/startedAt) is extracted to an exported pure `parseRollupEntries(raw: unknown): PrRow["statusCheckRollup"]` that parsePrRows calls; pr-gate feeds the raw `statusCheckRollup` of each open-PR row through it before foldRollup. parsePrRows' output is byte-identical to today for every input; pr-gate never casts raw gh JSON to RollupEntry.

INV-6 (one required-contexts parser, wire untouched): TurnSnapshotGithub.requiredStatusContexts() keeps issuing exactly `gh api repos/<repo>/branches/master/protection/required_status_checks --jq .contexts` — the argv is pinned by `expected.ghCalls` in 81+ goldens, so the port does NOT switch to the raw payload. pr-gate adapts the post-jq read to the parser's shape with a one-line wrap: empty read → DEGRADE.EMPTY_PAYLOAD, unparseable → DEGRADE.UNPARSEABLE (both as today), otherwise `parseRequiredStatusContexts({ contexts: read.data })`; `null` → healthy empty set (golden failure-required-contexts-null-healthy), an array → its non-empty string members, and a parser `null` (contexts present but neither null nor an array) → `{ ok: false, reason: DEGRADE.MALFORMED_PAYLOAD }`. The last arm is a deliberate fail-closed tightening of today's 'other JSON → healthy empty set' (#4460 INV-5 direction); no golden on master exercises it (observed required-read stdouts: a 7-name array ×81, `[]` ×7, `null` ×1, `not json` ×1, empty ×3), so it flips no golden and is recorded in the PR body as a non-golden behaviour change.

INV-7 (goldens are the contract): every file under test/fixtures/turn-snapshot/ and test/fixtures/turn-snapshot-parity/ is byte-identical on this PR — no re-record, no hand edit, no new fixture. If any golden flips under the design above, the fix is in the port/adapter code, never in the fixture; the PR body lists each such fixture as a candidate behaviour change for a separate issue (the issue's rule), and the expected count of such fixtures is zero given INV-2/INV-3/INV-6's corpus scan.

INV-8 (test accounting): the collector-level pr-gate tests (test/turn-snapshot-pr-gate.test.mts, incl. the CANCELLED-latest, advisory-never-qualifies, pending-disqualifies and StatusContext-FAILURE cases) are kept — they pin the WIRING's observable output and would catch a dropped `started-only`; the fold-level semantics they relied on gain 1:1 cases in test/github-check-rollup.test.mts (started-only picks the later-startedAt CANCELLED over an earlier FAILURE → not red; isSettled over absent / pending / cancelled / green required contexts; red+pending → isRed true, isSettled false). The suite-count baseline is regenerated with `--only` for the test files whose counts changed, in the same PR.

INV-9 (port-read guard): the number and order of port reads per turn is unchanged (test 'port read-count + order guard (#4941)' stays green): exactly five reads with no UNKNOWN, six with one; no new gh call, no removed call.

INV-10 (layering + docs): src/github/check-rollup.ts still imports only `type { PrRow }`; pr-gate imports from ../../github/check-rollup.ts and ../../github/prs.ts (both already-permitted downward edges — pr-gate already imports ../../github/pr-refs.ts). src/autopilot/CONTEXT.md's Turn Snapshot row gains one sentence: pr-gate's required-check verdict is the shared src/github/check-rollup.ts fold (started-only order, isRed + isSettled); ADR-0043 D4's wire-parity constraint pins the port's gh argv (the goldens record ghCalls), not a private fold. No ADR is edited.

INV-11 (verification): npm test, npm run typecheck and npm run typecheck:test pass; the PR's `Tier: 3` line and reconciliation section are present before the LAST push (design-concept-reconcile reads the push-time body).

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Port returns the raw branch-protection payload (drop `--jq .contexts`) and pr-gate calls parseRequiredStatusContexts on it directly
rejectedAlternatives.why: The goldens record exact gh argv in `expected.ghCalls` for every scenario that reaches the required read (81+ files). Dropping the jq flag changes the recorded argv and breaks byte-identity on the whole corpus — the issue's non-negotiable contract. Wrapping the post-jq value as `{contexts: data}` costs one line and keeps the wire untouched; the parser's fail-closed arm still applies.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Pass the fold's default `completed-then-started` order and only switch to `started-only` if a golden flips
rejectedAlternatives.why: No golden carries a completedAt, so the corpus cannot distinguish the two orders — a green run under the default would prove nothing and silently change the brain's rule the first time gh emits completedAt in production. The brain's rule is started-only (#4460); pin it in code unconditionally.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Compute `settled` inline in pr-gate by iterating fold.contexts for status === 'pending' instead of adding isSettled to the fold
rejectedAlternatives.why: That re-creates a private predicate over the fold's status table in the consumer — the pattern this epic is deleting. A named `isSettled` next to isRed/blocksMerge keeps the vocabulary (red / blocks-merge / settled) in one module and is reusable by slice 2's feed classifier.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Cast pr-gate's raw rollup rows to RollupEntry (filter non-objects with the existing asRow and `as` the rest)
rejectedAlternatives.why: The fold is typed over PrRow's normalised entry shape; a cast re-introduces the unparsed-gh-JSON hazard the normaliser in parsePrRows exists to close (non-string fields, nested shapes). Extracting parseRollupEntries from parsePrRows is a pure refactor that gives both callers the same normaliser.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Delete the collector-level rollup tests from test/turn-snapshot-pr-gate.test.mts ('move 1:1' read literally as move-and-remove)
rejectedAlternatives.why: Those cases exercise classifyPrGate's wiring (that pr-gate passes started-only and the required set); removing them leaves no non-golden guard on the wiring, and ADR-0043 D4 forbids suite-shrinking ports. Keep them; add the fold-level 1:1 cases where the semantics now live.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Keep today's 'non-array required payload → healthy empty set' arm when adapting to the shared parser
rejectedAlternatives.why: It would need a second parser rule living in pr-gate (violating 'exactly one required-contexts parser'), and it is the less safe semantics: an unexpected shape inventing an empty required set makes every red check non-required. prs.ts already decided malformed → UNKNOWN (#4569); the brain fails closed on it like every other INV-5 input.

qaTrace.q: Premise check against origin/master (f0365f6d4): is slice 1 shipped, are the pr-gate privates still present, is there an open PR for #5089, and is the blocked-by clear?
qaTrace.a: Yes on all four. src/github/check-rollup.ts exists (merged via PR #5207, issue #5087 CLOSED) exporting RollupOrder 'completed-then-started' | 'started-only', foldRollup({required, order}), classifyRollupEntry, collapseRollup, isRed, blocksMerge. pr-gate.ts still carries RED_CONCLUSIONS (:370), rollupLatest (:377, startedAt-only, ties → later index), requiredVerdict (:404, null when any required context is missing or pending), parseRequiredContexts (:709, post-jq array; null/other JSON → healthy empty set). github-port.ts requiredStatusContexts() issues `gh api .../protection/required_status_checks --jq .contexts`. No open PR references #5088 or #5089; #5088 (slice 2) is open with no PR, and this slice does not depend on it (stalled-prs.ts is out of scope here). Not fixed, not a duplicate — proceed.

qaTrace.q: Does the port expose the raw branch-protection payload, or keep `--jq .contexts` and adapt in pr-gate? (the question the issue leaves to the grill)
qaTrace.a: Keep the wire. Fact from the fixtures: every root golden records `expected.ghCalls` — exact argv in order — and 81+ scenarios reach the required read, so changing the argv is a corpus-wide golden flip. pr-gate therefore wraps the post-jq value: `parseRequiredStatusContexts({ contexts: read.data })`. Observed required-read stdouts across all goldens: a 7-name array ×81, `[]` ×7, `null` ×1, `not json` ×1, empty ×3 — the wrap reproduces each (null → [] healthy; array → strings; unparseable/empty → degraded as today). The parser's extra arm (contexts neither null nor array → null) maps to DEGRADE.MALFORMED_PAYLOAD; no golden exercises it, so it is a fail-closed tightening recorded in the PR body, not a golden change.

qaTrace.q: Which fold order does pr-gate pass — the default, or `started-only`, and conditionally or always?
qaTrace.a: `started-only`, always. The issue's 'pass the tie-break parameter where a fixture would flip' cannot be applied empirically: a scan of all 93 root goldens found 0 rollup entries with completedAt, so the default order and started-only produce identical results on the corpus and a green run under the default would be vacuous. The brain's rule is startedAt-only (#4460 INV-4 docblock on rollupLatest); pinning it in code is the only way behaviour is preserved beyond the corpus. The PR body still lists any golden that flips under the default order as a candidate behaviour change (expected: none).

qaTrace.q: How do requiredVerdict's three outcomes (null / {red:false} / {red:true}) map onto the fold without changing any verdict?
qaTrace.a: requiredVerdict is null iff some required name is absent from the latest-per-context map or some winning entry is pending. foldRollup({required}) represents an absent required context as status 'pending' with entry undefined (INV-6 of #5087), so 'null' ≡ 'some context pending'. The fold exposes isRed and blocksMerge but no pending-only predicate (blocksMerge also counts red and cancelled, and pr-gate treats CANCELLED as settled-not-red), so add `isSettled(fold)` = no context pending. Then settled = isSettled(fold); red = settled && isRed(fold). Edge checked: red + pending → today null (red=false, settled=false); with the composition red=false, settled=false. Identical.

qaTrace.q: Do the fold's per-entry classification rules differ from rollupLatest's on any golden? (status-ignoring conclusion test vs pr-gate's `status !== COMPLETED` pending rule; name keying; timestamp parsing)
qaTrace.a: Enumerated the divergences and scanned the corpus for each: (a) a CheckRun with status COMPLETED and a conclusion outside the red/green/cancelled sets (e.g. STALE) is settled-not-red today but pending in the fold — 0 goldens; (b) a non-COMPLETED CheckRun carrying a conclusion — 0; (c) a StatusContext state outside SUCCESS/FAILURE/ERROR/PENDING/EXPECTED/'' — 0; (d) nameless entries — 0, and under the required restriction a nameless/'check' entry can never match a required name anyway; (e) timestamps: pr-gate uses ghTimestampSeconds||0 vs the fold's plausibleTs (pre-2000 → -Infinity); both order a missing/sentinel stamp earliest with ties to the later index — only a missing-vs-0001 pair orders differently, 0 goldens. Conclusion: no golden flips; (a)–(e) are listed in the PR body as potential behaviour differences outside the corpus, for a separate issue if the operator wants the brain to track them.

qaTrace.q: pr-gate works on raw gh JSON rows (`unknown[]`), the fold on PrRow's normalised RollupEntry — where does normalisation live?
qaTrace.a: In src/github/prs.ts, once. parsePrRows already normalises statusCheckRollup inline (object-only entries; string-or-undefined conclusion/name/context/state/status/completedAt/startedAt). Extract it as an exported pure `parseRollupEntries(raw: unknown)` that parsePrRows calls (output byte-identical), and have pr-gate call it per PR row before foldRollup. The normaliser drops `__typename`; pr-gate's `"conclusion" in e || __typename === CheckRun` branch becomes the fold's 'non-empty conclusion string ⇒ CheckRun' rule — scan (b) above shows no golden where the two disagree.

qaTrace.q: What happens to the pr-gate tests the issue says 'move 1:1 to the fold's tests'?
qaTrace.a: Keep the collector-level cases in test/turn-snapshot-pr-gate.test.mts (they pin the wiring: dropping `started-only` or the required set would be caught there and in the goldens) and add the fold-level 1:1 cases to test/github-check-rollup.test.mts: started-only with a later-startedAt CANCELLED over an earlier FAILURE → not red; isSettled over absent / pending / cancelled / green; red+pending → isRed true, isSettled false. ADR-0043 D4 explicitly forbids suite-shrinking ports, so 'move' means 'the semantics are now pinned where they live', not 'delete from the consumer'. Regenerate the suite-count baseline with `--only` for the changed test files.

qaTrace.q: Does the change alter the per-turn port read count/order, the degraded markers, or any stderr note the goldens pin?
qaTrace.a: No. The same five reads (six with an UNKNOWN re-poll) are issued in the same order — the required read stays one call with the same argv (#4941 guard). The `requiredContexts` degraded marker keeps EMPTY_PAYLOAD / UNPARSEABLE for the two read failures; MALFORMED_PAYLOAD is added only for the parser-null arm no golden reaches. The stderr notes ('orch dev-resume required-contexts read FAILED (empty payload) …', 'orch dev-resume classifier fail-closed (dev-resume-input-unavailable) — issue #4460 INV-5') are emitted from the same sites with the same text.

qaTrace.q: Glossary: does the issue introduce terms missing from CONTEXT.md, and what documentation changes?
qaTrace.a: No gaps. Turn Snapshot, Pre-merge Gate, GitHub Issue/PR Read and Autopilot Run are all defined in CONTEXT.md; 'check-rollup fold', 'four-way status' and 'required contexts' are module-level names already carried by src/github/check-rollup.ts's docblock and #5087's approved artifact, not new domain vocabulary. Doc change: one sentence in src/autopilot/CONTEXT.md's Turn Snapshot row (shared fold, started-only, isRed + isSettled; D4 pins the port's argv not a private fold). No ADR edit — the epic says so and ADR-0043's decisions are unchanged (the port is still byte-identical on the wire).

qaTrace.q: Any interaction with slice 2 (#5088) or files out of scope?
qaTrace.a: src/aggregators/stalled-prs.ts stays untouched (out of scope). Both slices extend src/github/check-rollup.ts and test/github-check-rollup.test.mts, so whichever lands second may need a trivial rebase; isSettled is additive and useful to the feed too. Verifier-Core paths are not touched: pr-gate.ts, github-port.ts, prs.ts, check-rollup.ts are all T3 ('Core src/'), matching `Expected tier: 3`.
